actions.oldValue: Two hedgehogs confront survival, love, and an uncertain winter in dark woodland satire. Set in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, Day of the Hog follows two hedgehogs preparing for Groundhog Day as the prospect of six more weeks of winter threatens their home and survival. What begins as an absurdist woodland comedy gradually narrows its focus to the pressures of scarcity, partnership, and endurance as the shadow of Punxsutawney Phil hangs over their future. The play is a new work that blends animal fable, dark comedy, and social satire. Through the perspective of its hedgehog protagonists, the story examines how larger systems and traditions shape the lives of those with little power to influence them. actions.oldValue: A fast-paced adaptation of Chekhov exploring depression, misunderstanding, and human connection. Nikolai Ivanov, once admired and full of promise, finds himself overwhelmed by depression as those around him attempt to explain his unhappiness. Over the course of a year, conflicting assumptions, strained relationships, and missed connections expose the comic and tragic consequences of people failing to understand one another. This adaptation of Anton Chekhov's Ivanov presents the playwright's first major work in a contemporary, fast-moving form. The production is adapted and directed by Laura Strausfeld, whose version remains faithful to Chekhov's original while emphasizing its pace and wit.
